evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, contexts, values and planned diagrams are original. 9702_m24_22_q01_c directly grounds power-area intensity calculation. The other canonically mapped leaves contain amplitude demands reserved for Lesson 8 and are recorded as deferred rather than used here.

questions.prompt: State what is meant by wave intensity and give its SI unit.
A graph has displacement on the vertical axis and distance on the horizontal axis. What does the graph show?

options.A: The displacement of one chosen particle at successive times
options.B: The energy transferred by each particle during one period
options.C: The displacements of particles at different positions at one instant
options.D: The path followed by one particle as the wave travels

questions.prompt: A wave transfers 24 W uniformly through an area of 6.0 m² normal to the energy transfer. What is the intensity?
The same wave power is spread uniformly over a larger area. Which change occurs?

options.A: The power must increase and the intensity stays constant.
options.B: The power must decrease and the intensity stays constant.
options.C: The intensity increases because more area receives the wave.
options.D: The intensity decreases because the power per unit area is smaller.

questions.prompt: A uniform wave beam transfers 36 W through a rectangular cross-section 0.30 m wide and 0.20 m high. The cross-section is normal to the direction of energy transfer.

figure.purpose: Assess selection of the normal cross-sectional area before calculating intensity.
figure.brief: Original black-and-white line diagram of a rectangular beam cross-section labelled width 0.30 m and height 0.20 m, with energy-transfer arrows perpendicular to it. Do not include formulas or an area value.
figure.alt_text: A rectangular wave beam cross-section is 0.30 metres by 0.20 metres and normal to energy flow.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the area normal to the energy transfer.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the intensity of the wave beam.

questions.prompt: A small source transfers wave energy at a constant rate of 80 W. At a particular distance, the power is distributed uniformly over a complete spherical surface of radius 4.0 m.

figure.purpose: Assess a two-stage calculation from explicitly supplied spherical geometry and interpretation of local intensity.
figure.brief: Original black-and-white line diagram of a source at the centre of a complete sphere. Label radius 4.0 m and total power 80 W. Mark a 1 m squared patch on the sphere without giving the answer.
figure.alt_text: An 80 watt source is centred in a spherical surface of radius 4.0 metres.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the area of the spherical surface.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the wave intensity at this surface.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Explain why the intensity may be smaller at a larger spherical surface even though the source power remains 80 W.

questions.prompt: A pulse of wave energy is sent along a channel. At a measuring frame, 15 J crosses a rectangular area 0.50 m by 0.40 m in 2.5 s. The area is normal to the energy transfer.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: State what is transferred by the progressive wave and explain what happens to the channel particles after the pulse has passed.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the average power transferred during the 2.5 s interval.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Calculate the average intensity at the measuring frame.
